transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-06-18
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 58 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Alvarez (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (NebulaPay Head of ML), Garrett Miles (Platform Eng Lead), Lena Zhou (Security)

Auto-summary (auto-gen, may be noisy): Demo covering prompt evals, regression alerts, and A/B comparisons. Customer wants private deploy for payments PII, concerned about latency and cost. Next: pricing, bench, security doc.

--- Topics covered: Eval setup; demo of Console + API; Optimize recommendations for batching; regression alerting flow; AB comparison playbook; pilot next steps.

Transcript body (timestamps approximate, transcription imperfect):

[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Maya from Redwood, AE on the account. Diego, our solutions engineer, will run through the demo then we'll jump into questions.
[00:07] Diego: Hey, hi, all — Diego A. I'll show the Console flow and then the API benchmark. Quick ask, Priya, do you want us to focus on the prompt set design side or the AB compare first?
[00:18] Priya: Uh, both, I think. We've been seeing a few regressions in our payment chat flows, like amount parsing and chargeback classifi — classification, so we want to be able to detect regressions and run quick A/B checks when we change models or prompts. Also, latency's a problem during peak auth windows.
[00:33] Garrett: Yeah, and top constraint for us is PCI-compliance-ish stuff, we need strong encryption and control, so Private deployment or VPC options are basically required. But we want to measure unit cost too, because of volume.
[00:46] Lena: And I'll add, we need audit logs, SSO, and KMS integration — we cannot move secrets out to a third party unmanaged key store.
[00:55] Maya: Great — that's exactly the kind of constraints we usually see. Today we'll walk through building a prompt set, hooking a regression alert, then doing an AB comparison split. We'll also show the benchmark tool for latency vs cost.

[01:12] Diego: Opening Console — bear with me, screen share is coming. (murmur) Okay, on the left is Evalops, we have a project for NebulaPay. First step, prompt sets. We typically create canonical prompt families — dev, edge, and safety suites. Here's a prompt set for 'amount extraction' — sample prompts, expected tokens and labels.
[01:33] Diego: Note: transcripts sometimes show 'K-V cash' instead of 'KV cache' — sorry if that shows up in the UI text.
[01:40] Priya: (laughs) we've seen the K-V cash in other systems, it is what it is. On the prompt sets, can we upload CSVs with gold labels?
[01:46] Diego: Yes, CSV or JSONL. You can map fields to label columns. You can also add variants to test small template changes.
[01:53] Priya: Perfect. We will share three canonical prompt sets for the pilot: parsing, intent, and safety filters.

[02:03] Diego: Next, regression alerts. We have metric thresholds and soft-guardrails. Example: if exact match for amount drops by 3% relative to baseline over last 1k calls, alert. You can tie alerts to a webhook or Slack.
[02:19] Garrett: How noisy are those alerts? We don't want pager fatigue.
[02:23] Diego: Good question. Alerts have a cooldown and require both absolute and relative thresholds — so you can set, say, 3% drop AND at least 50 failing requests before firing. Also you can route to a 'severity' channel.
[02:34] Priya: Do alerts support sample payloads so we can inspect failing cases?
[02:38] Diego: Yes — when an alert fires, the UI attaches representative examples, prompt, model output, and difference to baseline.

[02:46] Maya: Quick call-out about model variants: Redwood routes requests to compatible model variants automatically if a primary is unavailable. For the pilot you can pick an optimized quantized variant to save tokens.
[02:59] Priya: Speaking of tokens, what's a rough per-1000-call cost for the configs you showed? We're aiming for sub-$0.02 per inference ideally.
[03:07] Diego: It depends on sequence length and batch settings. For short prompts (<=64 tokens) using a quantized variant on Dedicated we typically see $0.008–0.015 per call in our benchmarks; hosted may be a bit higher but faster to start. We'll send tailored pricing.
[03:25] Garrett: Can we run a benchmark with our traffic profile? We want to replicate peak auth windows — spiky concurrent requests.
[03:32] Diego: Absolutely — Diego: we can run a benchmark harness. We ask for a 24h sample of anonymized traffic and target SLOs. We'll surface latency percentiles (p50/p95/p99) and token-cost metrics.
[03:44] Priya: Note we may have some PII in the transcripts — we'll sanitize before sharing.

[03:50] Lena: On the Private deployment side, what's the minimum footprint? We can't run huge clusters on prem.
[03:55] Maya: For Private you can start with a small pool, and Redwood supports per-customer autoscaling up to your capacity limits. For PCI-like workloads, many customers run Private control plane with customer-managed networking and HSM/KMS.
[04:08] Lena: Do you support AWS KMS + HSM integrations?
[04:11] Diego: Yes — KMS integration is supported, including customer keys and HSM-backed stores. We'll include an architecture diagram in the follow-up.

[04:18] Garrett: If we do Dedicated reserved capacity, what's the SLA?
[04:22] Maya: Reserved Dedicated comes with an SLA aligned to throughput/latency targets. We'll put the SLA numbers in the SOW. For the pilot we usually run without a full SLA but with agreed performance targets.

[04:34] Priya: Back to the A/B comparison — show how we do statistical significance and guard against small-sample noise.
[04:39] Diego: Sure — the AB compare flow lets you define splits (50/50, 90/10) and connect multiple metrics: accuracy, F1, token usage, latency. We compute lift with bootstrapped confidence intervals and annotate drift over time.
[04:53] Priya: Can we compare across model families? Like Llama2 variants vs. an in-house tuned model?
[04:58] Diego: Yes, as long as the model is onboarded into the runtime or you provide a compatible endpoint. For private/on-prem you can register a local variant into the catalog and the AB runner will treat it like any other model.

[05:10] Garrett: Does the AB runner accept custom scoring functions? We have a heuristic scorer for amount rounding.
[05:15] Diego: You can upload a scoring script or run client-side scoring and push back evaluated labels. We support pairwise comparison as well.

[05:24] Maya: Quick demo: I create an AB experiment — name it 'amount-extraction-compare' — set metrics: exact_match, p95_latency, token_cost. We pick a 70/30 split. Diego will start the run for 10k samples.
[05:37] Diego: Running now... (pause) the runner surfaces live throughput, p50/p95, and current lift. You can pause, rollback, or promote variants.
[05:46] Priya: Nice. If we see a negative lift on exact_match but better latency, can we set automated fallback policies?
[05:52] Diego: Yes — there are policy rules: if metric X drops below threshold then rollback; or route high-value calls to the higher-quality model while low-value traffic goes to cheaper variant.
[06:03] Garrett: That routing piece is interesting — could save cost during low-risk flows.
[06:08] Priya: A couple of practical things: we run fraud detection and authorization in the same pipeline — false positives are costly. We need to be able to tag high-value transactions and test AB splits specifically for those.
[06:20] Diego: You can set traffic rules based on metadata; we support header-based routing and request attributes so you can carve out a subset for targeted experiments.
[06:29] Lena: On logging, can we keep full request/response logs on-prem? Our legal team will insist.
[06:34] Maya: For Private, yes. For Hosted we retain minimal logs by default but you can opt into longer retention or push logs to your S3/Kafka. We'll include log retention options in the follow-up.

[06:45] Priya: One friction we've had with other vendors — alert false positives and difficulty reproducing failure cases. How easy is it to reproduce in the Console?
[06:54] Diego: Reproduction is a core part: each alert links to a replay button that replays the exact prompt+context against the model variant and shows diffs. We also store snapshot of the prompt set and model version used.
[07:05] Garrett: Licensing question — if we onboard a private variant, do we pay per-hosted token usage plus a platform fee?
[07:12] Maya: Private licensing typically includes a platform fee (monthly) and a compute/usage component. Dedicated reserved has commit-based pricing. We'll detail in pricing docs.

[07:20] Priya: For pilot success criteria, we propose: p95 latency < 250ms for auth path, exact_match >= 98% on amount parsing, regression alert false positive rate < 1% over a rolling window.
[07:32] Maya: Those are reasonable targets. We'll bake them into the pilot SLO.

[07:37] Diego: Quick note on Optimize recommendations — the system suggests batching and quantization profiles per-model and per-workload. For short prompts, aggressive batching can reduce cost but adds latency, Optimize will surface trade-offs.
[07:51] Priya: Can we get Optimize suggestions programmatically via API? We want to integrate them into our CI.
[07:57] Diego: Yes — Optimize exposes recommendations via API and you can annotate runs to accept suggested profiles automatically.

[08:05] (background chatter, someone typing)
[08:10] Maya: Should we talk timeline? Priya, you mentioned pilot in July — is that still target?
[08:15] Priya: We were hoping to start a constrained pilot end of June / early July. We need security sign-off first though.
[08:21] Lena: I'll need the SOC2 docs, network diagram, and details on key rotation. Also vendor risk questionnaire answers.
[08:27] Maya: We'll send SOC2, architecture diagram, and a filled vendor risk questionnaire. We'll also include KMS integration notes.

[08:35] Garrett: One more operational question — when an AB run shows degradation, do you provide a rollout automatic rollback or manual?
[08:42] Diego: Both. You can set auto-rollback thresholds, but most customers start with manual review then move to auto as confidence grows.
[08:50] Priya: What about model drift detection over weeks — not just immediate regression after a deploy?
[08:56] Diego: We support long-term drift monitoring; you can attach alert rules that look at 7/14/30 day windows and compare to baseline.
[09:05] Priya: Great. For the bench, we'll provide a 24-hour slice plus a high-concurrency synthetic window. Diego, please include instructions on how to anonymize PII before upload.
[09:16] Diego: I'll add a step-by-step. We'll also provide a small harness to replay traffic with preserved timing.

[09:24] (slight feedback, pause)
[09:28] Maya: Ok let's do a quick recap of next steps. Maya to send Dedicated pricing and SOW; Diego to set up benchmark harness and share data upload link; Priya will share prompt sets and SLOs; Lena will provide compliance requirements and KMS vendor. Aim to have pilot kickoff week of 2027-06-28.
[09:48] Priya: Sounds good. Also, one last question: competitors — we've been talking to Anthropic and OpenAI about managed endpoints; how does Redwood differentiate on costs and private deploy?
[09:57] Maya: Short answer: we focus on production economics and private deployment options. We have first-class Dedicated and Private modes with routing and fallback controls. We'll include comparative notes in the follow-up.
[10:09] Garrett: Thanks everyone.
[10:12] Lena: Thanks.
[10:13] Diego: Thanks, we'll follow up with the materials.
[10:15] Maya: Bye all.

End of transcript.

Notes / artifacts referenced: Console demo (Evalops project), sample prompt sets (CSV), benchmark harness repo link (to be sent), SOC2 + arch diagram (to be sent).
